complexity.notes: Correctness is fine but the algorithm is impractical; the canonical monotonic-stack solution achieves the same O(n) with a small constant. Also, reusing the variable 'largest' for both the maximum bar height and the best area found is confusing — a separate variable would improve readability.
complexity.summary: Brute-force sweep: for every integer height h from 0 to max(heights), it makes one linear pass finding the widest run of bars with height >= h and tracks the best area. Since heights are bounded by 10000, this is at most 10001 linear passes, i.e. O(n) in n but with an enormous constant (~10^9 operations at n=10^5), so it will time out in practice despite being linear.
